headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow confusion: AutoGPT can read/write files and use network egress, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable docs list with no execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and use agent-protocol APIs, so if its outputs are manually copied into awesome-selfhosted notes or generated content, prompt-like text could be misread. However, awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and exposes no execution surface, so the bridge is weak and mostly manual.
conditions: IF an operator copies AutoGPT-generated text into awesome-selfhosted content or prompts
IF awesome-selfhosted content is later fed back into AutoGPT as instructions
mitigations: Keep a strict human review step before reusing AutoGPT output
Do not paste repository content directly into agent prompts
Use a separate scratch file for intermediate text
Label copied content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has allowlisted egress, but the pair shows no shared workspace, no shared credentials, and awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no data classes touched. With no documented data flow between them, there is no plausible leakage path in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or shared account is introduced outside the profiles
IF sensitive files are manually copied from AutoGPT into another system
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace
Keep secrets out of AutoGPT prompts
Use separate OS accounts
Review any manual export before sharing
requires-engineering: add DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, but awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely; any conflict would require an external orchestrator or manual workflow not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are placed on the same writable directory by an external orchestrator
IF awesome-selfhosted is converted into an editable workflow with write access
mitigations: Run them in separate directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use read-only access for awesome-selfhosted
Schedule sequential rather than parallel runs
requires-engineering: add file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate content that a human may copy into awesome-selfhosted, but awesome-selfhosted itself is a static knowledge-management repo and does not act on outputs. The cascade is therefore limited to mistaken curation rather than automated downstream action, and no direct verification pipeline is documented.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is treated as authoritative without human verification
IF generated text is committed into awesome-selfhosted without review
mitigations: Require manual fact-checking before commits
Compare outputs against source docs
Use a checklist for curation changes
Reject unverified claims from AutoGPT
requires-engineering: add citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is identified for either agent, and the profiles do not show residency, retention, or certification mismatches. AutoGPT touches no declared sensitive data, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable docs repository, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into AutoGPT workflows
IF the docs repository is repurposed to store regulated records
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems
Review repository contents before adding sensitive material
Use separate storage for compliance-scoped data
Document data classification rules
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
